title: Smart Salary Packaging: Converting Hourly Rates to Annual Pay Under the National Minimum Wage and Awards
description: Learn how to convert hourly pay to annual salary using the 38-hour week formula, understand the National Minimum Wage vs award rates, and explore smart salary packaging options.
salarySummary: For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52, with superannuation paid on top.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and an award rate?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage ($26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026) applies to employees not covered by an award or agreement. Award rates are minimum pay rates set by the Fair Work Commission for specific industries and occupations, and are often higher. Most employees are covered by an award. Use the Fair Work Ombudsman's pay guides to find the correct rate for your job.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the minimum hourly rate. For example, the National Minimum Wage for casuals is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 + 25%). When using the calculator, enter your base hourly rate (without loading) and check the casual loading box to add the 25% automatically.

faqs.q: What is smart salary packaging and how does it impact my take-home pay?
faqs.a: Smart salary packaging (also called salary sacrifice) lets you pay for certain items like a car or super contributions from your pre-tax salary, reducing your taxable income. The Fair Work Ombudsman explains that annualised wage arrangements can cover entitlements like penalties and allowances. However, our calculator does not deduct salary packaging; it shows gross pay and estimated tax without packaging. Consult a tax professional for personalised advice.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Hourly to Annual Conversion

If you're paid by the hour or considering a salary offer, converting your hourly rate to an annual figure helps you compare jobs and plan your budget. Our [the timesheet](/) calculator does this instantly, but it helps to know the maths behind it.

The standard formula is: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. We assume a 38-hour week, which is the full-time ordinary hours under the National Employment Standards. For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, annual gross pay is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,245.44.

A fortnightly figure is simply weekly pay × 2. For the same rate, weekly pay is $1,004.72, so fortnightly is $2,009.44. This can be useful for budgeting if you're paid fortnightly.

## National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour ($1,004.90 per week for 38 hours). This is the base rate for award/agreement-free employees. However, most Australian workers are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets higher minimum rates.

Award rates vary by industry and classification. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides pay guides for each award, listing minimum pay rates, allowances, and penalty rates. Always check the correct award for your job before relying on the National Minimum Wage.

### Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the minimum hourly rate. For the National Minimum Wage, that's $33.05 per hour. Our calculator includes a checkbox to add casual loading automatically. **Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – enter your base rate and let the tool add the loading.

## Smart Salary Packaging

Smart salary packaging (also called salary sacrifice) is an arrangement where you forgo part of your salary in exchange for benefits like a car, laptop, or additional super contributions. This reduces your taxable income, potentially lowering your tax bill. The Fair Work Ombudsman explains that some awards allow annualised wages to cover entitlements like penalties and allowances, but salary packaging is a separate contractual arrangement.

Our calculator does **not** deduct salary packaging. It shows your gross annual pay based on the hourly rate, then estimates tax and super. If you use salary packaging, your take-home pay will differ. For more details, see [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Tax and Superannuation

Tax is calculated using the 2026–27 resident rates:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income over $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. The calculator uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds (not yet confirmed for 2026–27).

Superannuation guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid **on top** of your salary. It does not reduce your take-home pay. The maximum contribution base is $270,830 per year. For example, on $52,245 annual pay, super is $6,269.40, bringing total employment cost to $58,514.84.

## Using the Calculator

Our [the timesheet](/) tool lets you enter your hourly rate, choose casual loading if applicable, and instantly see annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly pay. It also shows estimated tax and super. For more resources, explore [pay guides](/blog), [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage), [take-home pay](/topics/take-home), and [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading).

Remember: this is an estimate. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Always check your award or agreement for exact entitlements.

## Final Thoughts

Understanding how hourly rates translate to annual pay helps you negotiate salaries and compare job offers. Whether you're on the National Minimum Wage or an award rate, our calculator gives you a clear picture. And if you're considering smart salary packaging, talk to a professional to see how it affects your overall package.
